findings.title: Reject conservative drift before allocating the new head revision
findings.description: NativeWorkspace.submit delegates to NativeStore.submit after checking only selected source metadata. On a drifted module NativeStore fetches and JSON-decodes latest current metadata before checking reads=None. Thus a normal store head created through the existing unrestricted NativeStore API can exceed the workspace request_bytes metadata ceiling and still be allocated on a submission which must reject anyway. This is not a malicious concurrent-process scenario.

observed.result: Conflict: Unknown read dependencies after module drift: app

reproduce: Create app revision with edits {a: bytes(old)} using NativeStore.submit, base=None, reads=None.
Create NativeWorkspace(store, Limits(request_bytes=512)); materialize the old app revision to a fresh temporary snapshot.
Delete snapshot manifest, edit app/a to bytes(edit).
Advance app head through NativeStore.submit from the old base, adding extra0..extra199 each bytes(x).
Wrap native_store.json.loads with a delegating spy recording len(input.encode(UTF-8)); call workspace.submit with the original selected revision.
Observe 15683-byte current payload decoded before Conflict, despite 512-byte configured metadata ceiling.
findings.suggested_fix: Inside the existing transaction reject current != base with reads is None before loading latest. Retain request-key replay ordering and known read-set semantics. Add an allocation-bound regression asserting the new head is never decoded for conservative drift.

independent_adversarial.name: delta_exact_compact_item_byte_accounting
independent_adversarial.interpretation: Matches documented item-only budget; not a claim that total wire output fits page_bytes.

source_inspection: Sources come from caller-supplied exact selected closure; mutable manifest is never parsed for authority.
Every changed module uses reads=None; dependency changes remain pinned to old exact revisions by documented contract.
Source blob length and selected revision metadata length checked before full decode/read.
Filesystem entries and ancestors reject reparse points and symlinks; staging destination publication and cleanup exercised by existing real-filesystem fault-injection tests.
Cross-module receive and conflict use one native store transaction; existing suite confirms no partial head change.
Real empty-PATH subprocess CLI roundtrip and restart in existing suite rerun successfully.
Cursor is a deterministic input-bound position, not an authenticated access credential.

method_recall.applicable: bind-consumer-release: exact producer bytes and candidate bindings checked independently; mutated candidates require new receipt.
method_recall.counterexample: This review is not authority for downstream production/business acceptance.

limitations: Windows-only independent execution; Linux behavior not executed in this child.
Symlink privilege unavailable and FIFO platform skip are not passes.
Trusted single-writer local host assumption retained; no sandbox claim against malicious same-machine processes.
No complete production workflow integration, model token savings, commit, push, deploy or issue closure claimed.
Sources are uncommitted candidate files; HEAD alone is not the candidate binding.

cleanup.temporary_directory_policy: System TemporaryDirectory(prefix=duobao-independent-review-) removed on exit; junction explicitly removed before cleanup. Existing tests own their TemporaryDirectory cleanup.
